Evans-Jensen Classification of Intertrochanteric hip fractures

  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Definition

  • Based on the stability of the fracture after close reduction and skeletal traction
  • Describes fracture patterns as stable or unstable, based on the integrity of the posteromedial bony cortex. Stable fractures have intact or minimally comminuted posteromedial cortex, while unstable fractures has greater comminution of the posteromedial cortex
  • Unstable fractures after reduction can be converted to stable if the posteromedial opposition can be achieved
  • Reverse oblique pattern was considered inheritably unstable fracture as distal femur has tendency to drift medially due to adductor pull
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Classification

  • Grade 1 (Stable)
  • A: two part non displaced fracture
  • B: two part displaced
  • Grade 2 (Non stable)
  • A: three part fracture with separate grater trochanter fragment
  • B: three part fracture with separate lesser trochanter fragment
  • Grade 3 (Non stable)
  • four part fracture
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 1 A

  • Two part fracture
  • Non displaced
  • Stable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 1 B

  • Two part fracture
  • Displaced
  • Stable after reduction
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 2 A

  • Three part fracture with separate greater trochanteric fragment
  • Loss of posterolateral support provided by greater trochanter
  • Non stable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 2 B

  • Three part fracture with separate lesser trochanteric fragment
  • Loss of medial support provided by lesser trochanter
  • Non stable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden

Grade 3

  • Four part fracture
  • Include the reverse oblique fractures
  • Unstable
  • YouTube: Mustafa Salahalden
